name: Letta Code

surfaces.label: `letta` in a terminal, installed with npm, pnpm, bun, nvm, Homebrew node or Nix: the published package is one bundled JS file with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang (package.json bin letta -> letta.js), so ps shows `node <prefix>/bin/letta [flags]` with the SYMLINK path, not the real script (inferred, not seen). Docs require Node 22.19+, package.json engines also allows Bun >=1.3.2; the Nix flake wraps `bun $out/lib/letta-code/letta.js`, so `bun` is real for Nix (that form has no `bin/letta` argument and is the next surface). The same process runs the Ink TUI and the headless one-shot. Headless is vetoed by EXACT argument: `-p`/`--prompt` and every headless-only flag in src/cli/args.ts (`--output-format`, `--input-format`, `--run`, `--tags`, `--max-turns`, `--pre-load-skills`, ...; Herdr's is_interactive_letta_process rejects the same set). This matters because subagents are spawned with the prompt on STDIN, so their argv has NO `-p`: it is `letta.js --new-agent --system <type> --tags type:<t> --output-format stream-json --permission-mode unrestricted ...` (or `--conv <id>`), a direct child of the parent. `--output-format` is what vetoes them. Not vetoable by argv: a bare `letta` with stdin not a TTY and no prompt flag is also headless (isHeadlessStartup), and `--flag=value` spellings slip past exact matching. Management subcommands and their aliases (`upgrade`, `trajectory`, `--update`, `--upgrade`) are vetoed by exact argument, so a value equal to one (`letta -n memory`) hides a real session. Resume is `--conversation <id>` / `--conv <id>` / `-C <id>`; `--conv default --agent <id>` and `--conv <agent-id>` name an agent's default conversation, so the id is not always a conversation id; `--resume`/`-r` is a boolean that opens a selector and carries NO id. Plain `letta` carries no id in argv at all.

node or bun run directly on the real script path: npx cache, pnpm global (its shim execs `node <store>/@letta-ai/letta-code/letta.js`), the Nix wrapper (`bun $out/lib/letta-code/letta.js`, flake.nix line 80-87), a source-built copy. Same process shape and same vetoes as the symlink form. Subagents also resolve to this shape (the launcher runs argv[1] resolved to a real path), which is why the headless-flag vetoes must be here too.

`letta` installed from the PyPI wheel (`uv tool install letta`, `pipx install letta`): the Python launcher execve()s a bundled Node, so the pid is Node itself and argv[0] is the full path <site-packages>/letta_code/_payload/bin/node with argv[1] .../_payload/app/letta.js. Env LETTA_CODE_DISTRIBUTION=pypi. Note the old PyPI `letta` was the MemGPT server; that one runs under python, never under this path.

Letta desktop app (Letta.app, Electron built with ToDesktop, `Letta 0.32.19` at download.letta.com/mac/{dmg,zip}/arm64; macOS Apple Silicon only per docs). The main process is the GUI and holds the sleep assertion. It launches the agent harness as a child (next surface), so per-conversation state is not visible from this process. Electron helper processes live under Contents/Frameworks/ and do not match this path. `remote` is vetoed because the same executable runs the listener with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1.

Desktop listener WITH the title rewrite: the app spawns `<Letta.app>/Contents/MacOS/Letta --require <dist>/setProcessTitle.js <app.asar.unpacked>/node_modules/@letta-ai/letta-code/letta.js remote --env-name <name> --backend api|local` with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and setProcessTitle.js would rename it so ps reports `letta-code-listener` INSTEAD of those arguments. CORRECTED: the shipped Letta 0.32.19 app.asar contains NO setProcessTitle.js (dist/ holds only main.js, preload.js, fileOpsWorker.js, index.html, assets), and main.js only passes --require when existsSync(<__dirname>/setProcessTitle.js) is true, so this app version most likely runs the un-retitled form on the next surface. Kept for builds that ship the file; unverified either way without a running app. Up to three slots (desktop-primary, desktop-local-backend, desktop-direct-cloud). It is the App Server that runs the agent loop and the tool shells (direct children) for every conversation the app opens: many sessions per process. Its parent is the Letta main process, so the probe folds it into the GUI surface; it only reports on its own if the app died and left it orphaned.

Desktop listener WITHOUT the title rewrite, the expected shape for Letta 0.32.19 (setProcessTitle.js is absent from the shipped bundle, so the rename is skipped): argv is `<Letta.app>/Contents/MacOS/Letta <app.asar.unpacked>/node_modules/@letta-ai/letta-code/letta.js remote --env-name <name> --backend api|local` with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1. Read from dist/main.js of the downloaded app; never seen running. Its tool shells are direct children of this process.

`letta server` (cloud computer listener, `--computer-name`, `--channels`) and `letta server --listen [ws://host:port]` (App Server, WebSocket at /ws, many agents and conversations in one process; also `--openai-api`). npm/bin-symlink form. Runs the agent loop and tool shells itself.
`letta remote` (alias of `letta server`, older spelling; the desktop app itself uses `remote`). npm/bin-symlink form.
`letta server` run on the real script path (Nix wrapper `bun .../letta-code/letta.js server`, pnpm, npx, source build). Same meaning as the bin-symlink row above.
`letta remote` (alias of `letta server`) run on the real script path.
`letta server` from the PyPI wheel (bundled Node path).
`letta remote` from the PyPI wheel (bundled Node path).

Letta Cloud agents: chat.letta.com (web and mobile), cloud sandboxes, the native Slack integration, GitHub Action (letta-code-action). State and inference are server-side; the local process, if any, is one of the surfaces above acting as a 'computer'. Nothing to observe on this Mac.

working_signals.meaning: Desktop app only. Owner: the main Letta desktop process (not by letta-code-listener). No `name` filter on purpose: the probe tests `name in <pmset assertion name>`, and the real pmset name of an Electron `prevent-app-suspension` blocker is unverified, so any prose here could never match. The signal therefore counts any non-caffeinate assertion held by the Letta process tree, which can include Chromium's own (media). ProcessingSleepInhibitor starts the blocker on IPC set-processing-state(true) from a renderer, refreshes it as a 10 s heartbeat, and stops it on set-processing-state(false) or heartbeat timeout, so it tracks 'a renderer reports an active run', per window. Source is the shipped app.asar (dist/main.js), not public. The pmset assertion name is unverified and the renderer call site was not found in the bundle, so whether a pending approval keeps it held is unknown. The terminal CLI takes NO assertion and spawns no caffeinate.

CLI, `letta server` and any surface whose process runs the loop: the Bash tool spawns `/bin/zsh -c <cmd>` (`-lc` when login) as a DIRECT detached child on macOS (zsh is always tried first, then $SHELL), and it stays for the whole command. Only shell tools show up; Read, Edit, Write, Grep and every model call run in-process. Zsh may exec a lone command in place, so the child can then be `npm` or `git`, not a shell. Long-lived direct children exist: MCP servers, LSP servers (opt-in LETTA_ENABLE_LSP), and a same-executable `letta.js -p ... stream-json` child per running subagent. The updater's `npm install -g` is an execFile child, not a shell. In the desktop app the shells are children of letta-code-listener, two levels below the Letta main process, so this signal is blind there.

Local backend only (`--backend local`, or the desktop 'local' mode): every message is appended to conversations/<base64url(key)>/messages.jsonl, key `default:<agentId>` or `conversation:<conversation-id>`. The directory name is base64url, so the probe's {session_id} template cannot address one file and this signal cannot fire under the probe. The DEFAULT backend is Letta Cloud, which writes NO local transcript. Raises working, never proves idle. A second, weaker mtime for the TUI on either backend: ~/.letta/logs/chunk-logs/<agentId>/<Date.now()-rand>.jsonl is rewritten once per drained stream, and ~/.letta/logs/debug/<agentId>/<same>.log is appended by debugLog (the debug log is skipped when LETTA_CODE_TELEM=0; the chunk log is NOT, it has no such check); the session id is random per process and appears nowhere in argv.
Fallback. Guess: nothing was measured (no live instance). A network wait burns none. The desktop Electron tree also burns CPU when idle, so use 10 for the GUI surface.

Exact but not readable from ps: connect to a `letta server --listen` WebSocket (/ws), send runtime_start, and read update_loop_status. LoopStatus: SENDING_API_REQUEST, WAITING_FOR_API_RESPONSE, RETRYING_API_REQUEST, PROCESSING_API_RESPONSE, EXECUTING_CLIENT_SIDE_TOOL, EXECUTING_COMMAND = a turn is running; WAITING_ON_APPROVAL, WAITING_ON_INPUT = blocked on the human. Also a stream_delta with message_type stop_reason (other than requires_approval) ends a turn. Loopback listeners need no auth; a subscriber is a new client of a private app, so do not attach without the owner's consent. The probe cannot evaluate socket_activity.

waiting_signals.meaning: The TUI writes the terminal title (OSC 0) itself, on by default (default items: activity, agent-name). Working: the title starts with a one Braille spinner frame of ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏ (10 frames, 100 ms). Blocked on the human: the title alternates every 1 s between `[ ! ] Action Required` and `[ . ] Action Required` (pending tool approval or arena vote), replacing the spinner. Ready: no spinner. The spinner also runs for 'Starting', `!` bash mode and slash commands, so it is a broader 'busy' than a model turn. Read it from the host terminal or multiplexer (tmux pane_title, cmux, kitty, iTerm2), not from ps. Users can change the fields with /title; an explicitly empty list disables it.

While an approval or question dialog is mounted (Bash, file-edit, task, generic, question), the TUI writes OSC 9;4;3;0 (indeterminate progress) and OSC 9;4;0;0 (clear) when it unmounts. Herdr reads this as blocked. It is NOT emitted during a normal turn, so absence means nothing.

Legacy hooks (deprecated) only. The TUI calls sendDesktopNotification, which writes BEL and runs Notification hooks with message `Approval needed` (blocked) or `Turn completed, awaiting your input` (idle), plus `Stream error`, `Execution error`, `Processing error` at level error. Tell them apart by the message text.
Legacy hooks only: runs when a permission dialog appears; can allow or deny.
Listener and desktop App Server. Authoritative, but needs a WebSocket subscriber. Also `stop_reason: requires_approval` in a stream_delta.

hooks.config: DEPRECATED, may be removed: `hooks` key in ~/.letta/settings.json, .letta/settings.json (committable) and .letta/settings.local.json (merged, local first); `hooks.disabled: true` turns them all off. Command and prompt hook types. Replacement: Mods, trusted JS/TS files in ~/.letta/mods/ or $MEMORY_DIR/mods/ (in-process, /reload, `letta --no-mods` to skip; diagnostics at ~/.letta/mods/diagnostics/latest.json) with events conversation_open, conversation_close, tool_start, tool_end, turn_start, turn_end, llm_start, llm_end, compact_start, compact_end (llm and compact events need the local backend). Desktop listeners support mod tool/turn events but not conversation lifecycle events.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry: no @opentelemetry dependency and no OTEL_ or OTLP string in the source or the docs. The only telemetry is Letta's own product analytics (session_start, session_end, tool_usage, error, user_input events) posted to the Letta API /v1/metadata/telemetry; opt out with LETTA_CODE_TELEM=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Nothing a local monitor can read.

notes: Not installed here; nothing seen running, so no live claim. Per-process turn state is exposed by only three things: the terminal title (spinner vs `[ ! ] Action Required`), a direct `/bin/zsh -c` child while a shell tool runs, and, for the desktop app, a power assertion on the main process. The CLI has no sleep inhibitor, no caffeinate, no lock file and no pid registry; its session id is random per process and not in argv, so map a TUI process to a conversation by --conversation/--conv when given, otherwise by cwd + newest file, or by the environment of a tool shell it is running (children get LETTA_CONVERSATION_ID, LETTA_AGENT_ID, AGENT_ID, CONVERSATION_ID, MEMORY_DIR, USER_CWD). The default backend is Letta Cloud, so a signed-in install has no local transcript at all. Headless runs and subagents are one-shots: alive means working, but they are vetoed from the TUI surface by exact arguments (`-p`, `--prompt`, `--output-format`, `--input-format`, `--run`, `--tags`, ...) because a substring rule for `-p` would also match `--permission-mode` and any path with `-p`. Subagents carry NO `-p` (prompt goes on stdin), so `--output-format` is the veto that catches them. A piped `echo x | letta` with no flag is headless too and is NOT vetoed. Matching reads argv only: `letta server` is matched by the substring `server`, so a TUI run as `letta -n api-server` is misfiled as a daemon. The desktop listener's tool shells are grandchildren of the app, so read it through the app's power assertion, not tool_children. The listener is probably NOT retitled `letta-code-listener` in 0.32.19 (setProcessTitle.js is missing from the bundle); the un-retitled `Letta <...>/letta.js remote` surface is the expected one. The bare `bin/letta` substring also matches any node script whose path contains `bin/letta...`; nothing else was found to collide, and the old MemGPT `letta` runs under python.
